title: Model a proof faithfully as a dependency graph of step nodes (blueprint node)
intent: Prescribe how to turn a root theorem's proof into a source-level dependency graph: the root is author-frozen before its proof, the proof is modelled as a conjunction of substantive step nodes consumed through a DEPS edge set, and the glue is the edges, one direct-use locator per edge — so a later Lean orchestrator gets a checked skeleton with one bounded, independently failing obligation per step.

children.name: step-node-nontrivial-estimate-or-construction
children.statement: a step node for a nontrivial estimate or construction — one of the substantive proof-step kinds the threshold names as "a nontrivial estimate, construction" (SKILL.md lines 192-193), created because omitting it would hide "a plausible Lean lemma or an independently failing obligation" (lines 191-192).
children.closed_by: the step's own proof, supplied by the later Lean orchestrator; this source-extraction skill only records the node and makes no claim that the proof is complete (SKILL.md lines 10-11).

applicability.goal_shape: A proof of a root theorem (an author-frozen, one-declaration anchor) that must be turned into a machine-checked dependency graph for a later Lean orchestrator, where the proof is line-addressable source (LaTeX or Markdown) and each substantive step can become one node.
applicability.use_when: you must trace a proof's dependencies at source level without deciding whether any theorem is proved; the root is already frozen as an exact Lean declaration (Phase 0, SKILL.md lines 63-107); you want a bounded number of lemma-sized step nodes per proof, each an independently failing obligation, plus explicit leaf nodes for standing assumptions and external results.
applicability.avoid_when: you are inspecting implementation Lean code or deciding whether a theorem is proved (the skill forbids this, SKILL.md lines 16-21); the step is routine algebra or a purely syntactic rewrite that changes no hypothesis, constant, carrier or quantifier strength (lines 195-196); or there is no author-frozen root anchor to root the graph.

claims.claim: The recorded theorem-scale shape is direct_lemmas = 5 (the five step-node kinds the site enumerates), depth = 1 (each step node is a direct leaf of the root and none depends on another), glue_lines = 51 (the parent site, SKILL.md lines 184-234), and child_lines = [6, 6, 6, 6, 6] (each child site is the threshold paragraph, lines 191-196).
claims.evidence: counted on the copied file: the parent site SKILL.md 184-234 spans 51 lines; each of the five child sites spans SKILL.md 191-196 (6 lines); the five step-node kinds are enumerated together in one sentence (lines 192-194) as sibling leaves below the root, with no step-node-to-step-node edge in the site, hence depth = 1.

claims.claim: The skill states the step-node threshold in its own words: "Create a step node when omitting the step would hide a plausible Lean lemma or an independently failing obligation", and excludes routine steps: "Do not create nodes for routine algebra or purely syntactic rewrites unless they change hypotheses, constants, carriers, or quantifier strength".

The skill keeps proof topology out of the statement: "Keep source-statement fields and proof topology separate. `DEPS` names results the source proof consumes; it never enlarges `SOURCE_HYPOTHESES`", and "Never use an edge to launder proof content into a statement".

metrics.how_counted: parent_lines = span of the parent site (SKILL.md 184-234); children = the five step-node kinds the threshold paragraph (191-196) enumerates, each given a child site of 6 lines; the skill is source-extraction only, so no child is closed here — the later Lean orchestrator closes them.

consequences: Creates obligations: every substantive step must become a node with a stable ID and statement/proof locators; every DEPS or ROUTES entry needs one EDGE record with a direct-use locator (the glue, SKILL.md lines 186-189 and the EDGE schema in DEPGRAPH.template.md); standing assumptions and external results must be explicit leaf nodes (lines 215-218). Failure modes the skill names: adding a prerequisite merely because it appears earlier in the paper (lines 186-187); putting alternatives in one comma-separated DEPS list instead of separate ROUTE nodes (lines 208-211); turning a theorem-local premise into a node (lines 220-221); and laundering proof content into a statement — DEPS must never enlarge SOURCE_HYPOTHESES (lines 229-234).
